• Core Course (CC)-MG2CCRBBA100-ORGANISATIONAL BEHAVIOUR
  • DURATION: 2 Hours Maximum Marks: 70
  • If at least two points in answer, or answer with relevant explanation should be given maximum
  • marks.
  • a)Apply sociological concept to suggest solutions to organisational behaviour
  • Here are some sociological concepts applied to organizational behaviour
  • Social Learning Theory: Use role models and mentoring to promote positive behaviours.
  • b)List and explain any three objectives of organisational behaviour with illustration.
  • (Give full marks even if no illustration is written), (Mark can be awarded for any objectives)
  • Here are three objectives of Organisational Behaviour
  • Understanding Employee Behaviour: To comprehend why employees behave in certain ways.
  • - Illustration: A manager understands an employee's tardiness is due to transportation issues.
  • Attitudes: Preconceived notions or biases
  • Example: A manager with a positive attitude towards teamwork is more likely to perceive a
  • collaborative effort as successful.
  • Environment: Physical surroundings influence perception
  • Example: A noisy office may lead to distractions and affect perception of work quality.
  • Changing priorities (e.g., family, health)
  • Greater self-awareness
  • Interpreting information
  • Autonomy (control over one's life)
  • Hygiene Factors: Basic needs (salary, job security, work conditions) that prevent dissatisfaction.
  • Openness to Experience: Curiosity, openness, and love for learning.
  • No one-size-fits-all approach: Leadership effectiveness depends on the situation.
  • Task-oriented leaders: Effective in structured tasks, but may struggle with ambiguous tasks.
  • Intelligence : Cognitive ability to process information, analyse situations, and make informed
  • decisions.
  • Virtual Collaboration: E-Teams work remotely, using digital communication tools to collaborate
  • and share information.
  • Common Goals: A marketing team forms to launch a new product, sharing the goal of increasing
  • sales.
  • Skill Enhancement: Developing individual skills and competencies to contribute to team success.
  • Forming: Establish clear goals, roles, and expectations. Introduce team members, define project
  • scope, and set timelines.
  • Self-Awareness: X recognizes her strengths (creativity, passion) and weaknesses (financial
  • management). She delegates tasks and seeks mentorship to fill gaps.
  • Improved Decision-Making: Self-awareness helps Sarah make informed decisions.
  • Values and Norms: Organisational culture defines acceptable behaviour, influencing employee
  • attitudes and actions.
  • Ethics and Integrity: A strong culture promotes ethical behaviour, accountability, and
  • transparency.
  • Anticipating Challenges : An employee, anticipating a project's potential roadblocks, proactively
  • develops contingency plans, ensuring timely completion.
  • Increased Productivity: Proactive self-leadership enables employees to manage tasks efficiently.
  • Building Trust and Understanding: Cross-cultural communication fosters trust by
  • demonstrating respect for different perspectives and acknowledging cultural variations.
questions.final_answer: demonstrating respect for different perspectives and acknowledging cultural variations.

questions.question: State and explain the systematic problem-solving strategies in Organisation Behaviour.
questions.solution_html:
• Symbolic Interactionism: Improve communication by being aware of nonverbal cues and
  • language.
  • Predicting Employee Behaviour: To forecast how employees will react in different situations.
  • - Illustration: A leader anticipates team resistance to changes and prepares a clear explanation.
  • a )Compare internal and external factors of perception with example .
  • (Give full marks even if there is no explanation)
  • Here's a comparison of internal and external factors of perception
  • Expectations: Prior experiences or expectations influence perception
  • Example: An employee expecting a promotion may perceive a meeting with the boss as an
  • opportunity for discussion.
  • External Factors
  • Social Influence: Others' opinions or behaviours influence perception
  • Example: Colleagues' positive feedback may influence an employee's perception of their work.
  • b)Explain how neuroticism impacts an individual.
  • Neuroticism can lead to increased anxiety, stress, and emotional instability, affecting an individual's
  • well-being, relationships, and overall quality of life. It may also impact their ability to cope with
  • challenges and make decisions.
  • (Mark can be awarded for any other related point/concept)
  • Reflecting on accomplishments and regrets
  • Refocused priorities
  • Making decisions
  • Competence (feeling effective and capable)
  • Motivator Factors: Growth needs (recognition, achievement, responsibility) that promote
  • satisfaction and motivation.
  • Conscientiousness: Organization, responsibility, and reliability.
  • Contextual factors: Leadership success is influenced by factors like task structure, leader-member
  • relations, and the leader's power.
  • People-oriented leaders: Effective in situations requiring teamwork and collaboration.
  • Confidence: Self-assurance and faith in one's abilities, inspiring trust and confidence in others.
  • Geographic Dispersion: Team members are located in different parts of the world, often across
  • multiple time zones.
  • Social Needs: Colleagues from different departments form a social group to support each other and
  • build relationships.
  • Personal Growth: Fostering self-awareness, confidence, and emotional intelligence to improve
  • teamwork and collaboration.
  • Storming: Manage conflicts, negotiate roles, and build trust. Encourage open communication
  • address disagreements, and clarify responsibilities.
  • Proactivity: X anticipates market trends, adapts her business strategy, and takes calculated risks to
  • stay ahead.
  • Increased Adaptability: Proactivity enables her to respond to changing circumstances.
  • Communication Styles: Culture affects how employees interact, collaborate, and resolve conflicts.
  • Innovation and Risk-Taking: A culture embracing experimentation and learning encourages
  • innovation.
  • Seeking Opportunities: A marketing specialist takes initiative to attend industry conferences
  • networking and staying updated on trends to drive business growth.
  • Improved Adaptability: Self-leaders adapt quickly to changing circumstances.
  • Facilitating Collaboration and Teamwork: Effective communication enables teams to
  • leverage diversity as a strength, promoting creativity and innovative problem-solving.
questions.final_answer: leverage diversity as a strength, promoting creativity and innovative problem-solving.
